description: Rhodium is a rare, dark silvery-white, hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with symbol Rh and atomic number 45. It is a noble metal and member of the platinum group, with only one naturally occurring isotope. It is one of the rarest and most valuable precious metals.
uses: Rhodium is primarily used as a catalyst in three-way catalytic converters in automobiles, consuming about 80% of world production. It is also used for enhancement of jewelry, electroplating on white gold and platinum, rhodium-plating of sterling silver to resist tarnishing, in catalytic processes for acetic acid production, asymmetric hydrogenation for drug precursors, and in neutron detectors for nuclear reactors.
characteristics: Rhodium is a hard, silvery, durable metal with high reflectance that does not normally form an oxide even when heated. It has both a higher melting point and lower density than platinum, and is not attacked by most acids, being completely insoluble in nitric acid and dissolving only slightly in aqua regia.
